title: EIP-8151: Account Code Restricted ecRecover
description: Restrict ecRecover results to accounts with empty code or a delegation indicator
author: Liyi Guo (@colinlyguo), Nicolas Consigny (@nconsigny)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract This EIP modifies the `ecRecover` precompile at address `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001` to apply the [EIP-3607](./eip-3607.md) account-code restriction, except for delegation indicators specified by [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md). After performing ECDSA public key recovery, the precompile returns the recovered address only if its current raw account code is empty, or exactly an EIP-7702 delegation indicator. Otherwise, it returns empty output, the same result `ecRecover` already returns when recovery fails. ## Motivation EOAs can use [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md) as a bridge to post-quantum authorization. After migration, the account has regular deployed code instead of an EIP-7702 delegation indicator `0xef0100 || delegate_address`, so [EIP-3607](./eip-3607.md) disables protocol-level ECDSA transaction origination. However, `ecRecover` ignores account state. A quantum-capable attacker deriving the old ECDSA private key could still authorize token transfers through contracts, including [ERC-20](./eip-20.md) `permit` implementations ([ERC-2612](./eip-2612.md)). This EIP applies the same rule to `ecRecover`: recovery returns empty output when the account has non-empty raw code that is not a valid EIP-7702 delegation indicator. As a result, after the account has migrated to post-quantum authorization, the old ECDSA private key can no longer be used for contract authorization that relies on `ecRecover`. ## Specification ### Modified `ecRecover` Behavior Starting at the activation of this EIP, the `ecRecover` precompile at address `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001` must perform the following steps. Recovery failure and a rejected code check both return empty output with `success = 1`. 1. Consume `3000` gas. If the gas is insufficient, halt for out of gas. 2. Perform ECDSA public key recovery from the input `(hash, v, r, s)` as currently specified. If recovery fails, return empty output. 3. If recovery succeeds, compute the code-check cost from [EIP-8038](./eip-8038.md). Cold or warm comes from `accessed_addresses`, before the account is read. This is the pre-state gas check from [EIP-7928](./eip-7928.md). - If `recovered_address` is absent from `accessed_addresses`, the account-access component is `COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS` (`3000` gas). Otherwise it is `WARM_ACCESS` (`100` gas). - Add one `WARM_ACCESS` (`100` gas) as the code-query fee. Empty code does not waive this fee, and a code check that later rejects the account does not waive it either. 4. Consume the code-check cost. If the gas is insufficient, halt for out of gas. This operation then makes no account access. 5. Add `recovered_address` to `accessed_addresses`, record the account read specified below, and read its raw code. 6. If that raw code is empty or exactly an EIP-7702 delegation indicator, return `recovered_address` left-padded to 32 bytes. 7. Otherwise, return empty output. ### Account Code Check The check uses the raw account code stored in state for `recovered_address`, without following a delegation indicator. An absent account is treated as having empty code. ```python code = state.get_raw_code(recovered_address) is_permitted = len(code) == 0 or (len(code) == 23 and code[:3] == bytes.fromhex("ef0100")) ``` Thus, the recovered address is returned only when its raw code is empty or exactly `0xef0100 || delegate_address`. ### Gas Cost When ECDSA recovery fails, no state access is performed and no fee is added to the base `3000` gas. When ECDSA recovery succeeds, the code-check cost is [EIP-8038](./eip-8038.md) `COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS` (`3000` gas) or `WARM_ACCESS` (`100` gas), plus one `WARM_ACCESS` (`100` gas) for the code query. That is `3100` gas cold and `200` gas warm. The total cost is `6100` gas cold and `3200` gas warm. The address is added to `accessed_addresses` only after this cost is paid, and it stays warm for later operations unless an enclosing scope reverts. ### Block Access List When [EIP-7928](./eip-7928.md) is active, paying the code-check cost is an account read of `recovered_address`: - Record the read only after that cost is paid. An out-of-gas code check contributes no account access. - The read is the raw code of `recovered_address`. Its delegation target is not loaded. - If the account has no other changes, include it with empty change lists. - A rejected code check leaves the read in place. An outer scope that later reverts also leaves the read in place. A reverted scope restores `accessed_addresses` to its contents on entry to that scope. Accesses that already existed stay. ### Public Mempool These rules apply only to public mempool validation of [EIP-8141](./eip-8141.md) frame transactions. They do not affect consensus. With this EIP, `ecRecover` reads the raw code of the address it recovers. A validation prefix that calls `ecRecover` therefore depends on the code of each address it recovers, and that address may be a third party rather than the sender. Only the outcome of the account code check matters. This section calls it the address's code class: permitted (empty code or an EIP-7702 delegation indicator) or rejected (any other code). Moving between empty code and a delegation indicator does not change the class. An address whose private key is known can change class by adopting code, for example with `SETCODEFROM` ([EIP-8298](./eip-8298.md)), and a reorg can change it back. #### Signer Dependencies While simulating the validation prefix, a node should record each address whose raw code `ecRecover` reads, together with its code class, as a signer dependency of the transaction. `tx.sender` is the exception: its code is already a dependency of the transaction, so recovering it adds no signer dependency. A node should revalidate a transaction when the code class of one of its signer dependencies at the new head differs from the recorded class.
